issues.legal_issue: A major person may marry or live with a person of their choice, including in an inter-caste or inter-religious relationship, and the marriage is not unlawful merely because it crosses caste or religious lines.
material_facts: The woman was a major and had left her brother’s home of her own free will.
She stated that she had married her chosen partner of her own free will and had a child with him.
The alleged opposition to the marriage arose because it was inter-caste.
issues.conclusion: A major is free to marry or live with anyone they choose. There is no legal bar to an inter-caste marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act or any other law, and no offence was committed merely by the woman’s voluntary marriage or by her husband and his relatives.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that a major’s choice of spouse or partner is free and that inter-caste or inter-religious marriage is not prohibited. It noted that neither the Hindu Marriage Act nor any other law bars an inter-caste marriage. No earlier cases were cited for this ruling.

predicates.adult_person: The person who chose the relationship had attained adulthood.
predicates.voluntary_choice_of_partner: The person chose the partner and entered the relationship of their own free will.
predicates.intergroup_relationship: The partners belonged to different caste or religious groups.

issues.definition: When an adult freely chooses a partner from a different caste or religious group, the marriage choice is lawful.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal prosecution founded on an allegation of kidnapping or abduction cannot be maintained where the adult concerned voluntarily left home and married, and the record shows no offence by the accused.
material_facts: The woman was a major when she left home and stated that she had done so of her own free will.
In a statement recorded by a magistrate, she said she had married voluntarily.
The police filed a final report stating that no offence had been committed by the accused.
A medical board found that she was not suffering from mental illness, despite a protest alleging that she was mentally unfit.
The prosecution nevertheless proceeded to committal and trial, and warrants were issued against the accused.
The Court considered the prosecution to have been initiated at the instance of the woman’s brothers, who were angry about her inter-caste marriage.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution was an abuse of the court process and administrative machinery. The Court allowed the writ petition, quashed the criminal proceedings and warrants, and held that no offence had been committed by the accused.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a major’s voluntary departure and marriage do not constitute an offence merely because relatives object to the marriage; a prosecution unsupported by an offence and used to harass the couple and their relatives is an abuse of process. The proceeding was brought under Article 32 of the Constitution, and the prosecution concerned alleged offences under sections 366 and 368 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases were cited for this ruling.

rule.if: writ_petition_to_quash_prosecution and adult_person and voluntary_departure_and_marriage and no_offence_disclosed

predicates.writ_petition_to_quash_prosecution: A person seeks relief in a proceeding asking the court to quash a criminal prosecution.
predicates.adult_person: The person whose departure or marriage is at issue had attained adulthood.
predicates.voluntary_departure_and_marriage: The adult left home and married of their own free will.
predicates.no_offence_disclosed: The record shows no offence committed by the accused in connection with the adult’s departure or marriage.

issues.definition: In a petition to quash a prosecution, if an adult voluntarily left home and married and the record discloses no offence by the accused, the prosecution is quashed.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities must protect adults who marry across caste or religious lines from harassment, threats and violence, and must take action against those responsible.
material_facts: The petition alleged that relatives opposed the woman’s inter-caste marriage and threatened the couple and their relatives.
The petition also alleged assaults, intimidation, detention of a relative, and interference with the husband’s family property.
The Court noted that reports of threats, harassment and violence against adults who marry outside their caste were occurring in several parts of the country.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed police and administrative authorities throughout the country to ensure that adult couples who marry across caste or religious lines are not harassed, threatened or subjected to violence, and to institute criminal proceedings and take stern action against those responsible in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that threats, harassment and violence against adults who voluntarily enter inter-caste or inter-religious marriages are wholly illegal. It stated that relatives who disapprove may end social relations but may not threaten, commit or instigate violence. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited as the basis for this general direction.

predicates.adult_intergroup_couple: Two adults entered a marriage across caste or religious lines.
predicates.threats_or_harassment_or_violence: A person threatened, harassed or committed violence against the couple because of their marriage.

issues.definition: When a person threatens, harasses or uses violence against an adult couple because they married across caste or religious lines, authorities must protect the couple and take action against the responsible person.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities must institute criminal proceedings in accordance with law against persons alleged to have committed unlawful acts against a couple and their relatives in reaction to the couple’s inter-caste marriage.
material_facts: The petition alleged that the woman’s brothers assaulted and threatened members of her husband’s family, took possession of property, and caused relatives to be arrested through a false kidnapping report.
The Court directed that criminal proceedings be instituted against the brothers and others involved in the alleged acts.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the concerned authorities to institute criminal proceedings forthwith against the woman’s brothers and others involved, in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed criminal proceedings on the basis of the allegations set out in the petition, while requiring that proceedings be conducted in accordance with law. No particular statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this direction.

predicates.court_proceeding_on_alleged_retaliation: A court is considering a matter in which alleged unlawful conduct is said to have been retaliation for a couple’s marriage.
predicates.alleged_unlawful_acts_against_couple_or_: The petition alleges that persons assaulted, threatened, unlawfully confined or dispossessed the couple or their relatives.

issues.definition: When a court considers alleged retaliatory unlawful acts against a couple or their relatives, the authorities must institute criminal proceedings in accordance with law.
